applicableAreas: Southern property boundary adjacent to overhead electric line
Western property boundary along Valley View Road
findings.comment: Plant schedule identifies four tree species proposed near overhead electric lines (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) but does not indicate utility-compatible (UC) designation per ECM Appendix F. ECM Appendix F is not provided in site plan documentation. Cannot determine whether proposed non-utility-compatible species are located within the 15-foot minimum clearance zone from distribution conductors without: (1) verification of UC status from Appendix F, and (2) lateral distance dimensions from tree trunk centers to conductors, which are not provided on any plan.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary adjacent to overhead electric line (25-foot zone from distribution conductor)
Western property boundary along Valley View Road (25-foot zone from distribution conductor)
findings.comment: Plant schedule shows only minimum specification planting heights (16' minimum for Live Oak and Cedar Elm; 10' for Mexican Redbud; 8' for Texas Mountain Laurel), not mature heights per ECM Appendix F. Landscape plan contains no designation or notation identifying which trees are 'large trees' (40+ feet mature height per ECM Appendix F). Cannot verify whether large trees are proposed within 25-foot clearance zone from distribution conductors without: (1) mature height specifications per Appendix F, and (2) lateral distance dimensions from tree trunk centers to conductors.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary adjacent to overhead electric poles
Western property boundary along Valley View Road (poles implied by overhead electric lines shown on electrical plan)
findings.comment: Landscape plan shows overhead electric lines but does not identify or label utility pole locations. Electrical plan shows OHE line along western boundary (Valley View Road) but does not show pole positions. Without pole locations marked on the landscape plan and lateral distance dimensions from tree trunk centers to poles, cannot verify whether trees are proposed within the 10-foot minimum clearance zone from utility poles.

applicableAreas: Areas with underground electrical transformers and pull boxes throughout the site
findings.comment: Electrical plan (Sheet 21) shows underground transformer pads and pull box locations throughout the site. Landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not display these underground equipment locations or cross-reference them to proposed tree locations. No lateral distance dimensions are provided showing clearance from tree trunk centers to underground equipment. Cannot verify whether trees are proposed within the 5-foot minimum clearance zone from underground electric equipment.

applicableAreas: Areas with underground electrical transformers and pull boxes within 20 feet of proposed trees
findings.comment: Landscape plan does not show underground equipment locations or clearance distances from proposed trees. Without lateral distance dimensions between tree trunk centers and underground equipment, cannot determine which trees are within 20-foot zone requiring root barriers. Additionally, landscape plan contains no root barrier detail specifications or notes indicating where root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, positioned 5 feet from equipment) are required and proposed.

applicableAreas: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) showing all proposed trees near electric facilities
findings.comment: Landscape plan identifies proposed trees only by functional category (M=Mitigation Tree, P=Parking Buffer Point Tree, SY=Street Yard Tree). Tree symbols on the landscape plan contain no species labels and no common or scientific names. While Sheet 35 contains a plant schedule listing species, the landscape plan provides no cross-reference mechanism to connect individual tree symbols to their corresponding species in the schedule. Trees cannot be identified by species directly from the landscape plan.

applicableAreas: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) showing trees near overhead electric facilities
findings.comment: Landscape plan contains no designation, notation, or symbol differentiation to identify large trees (mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F). Tree symbols are not labeled with mature height specifications. Plant schedule shows only minimum planting heights (e.g., '16' HT minimum'), which do not correspond to mature heights per Appendix F definitions. Large trees cannot be visually distinguished from small trees on the landscape plan, preventing verification of compliance with 25-foot clearance requirement from distribution conductors.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary where overhead electric line is present and trees are proposed
Western property boundary (Valley View Road) where overhead electric line exists but is not depicted on landscape plan
findings.comment: Landscape plan shows overhead electric line on southern boundary but provides no clearance dimensions, notes, or specifications describing the relationship between proposed trees and this utility line. Visual overlap between tree canopy symbols and the OHE line is not accompanied by distance callouts or explanatory notes. Western boundary overhead electric line shown on electrical plan is not depicted on the landscape plan, making it impossible to visually verify tree clearances in that area. Landscape plan does not establish a clear relationship between specific proposed trees and overhead electric facilities with sufficient clarity to verify clearance compliance per UCM § 1.10.10.4.

applicableAreas: Southern property boundary adjacent to overhead electric line (where trees appear to be planted in close proximity)
Western property boundary along Valley View Road
findings.comment: No documentation of written approval from Austin Energy is provided in the site plan or supplementary documents (master comment report, completeness check results, engineer's summary letter, project review form). If any proposed trees are located within restricted clearance zones (within 15 feet of distribution conductors, within 10 feet of utility poles, or within 5-10 feet of pad-mounted or underground equipment), written approval from Austin Energy authorizing the variation must be provided and is not present in the submitted materials.
